$comment: Known, accepted violations. Anything not listed here fails the run.
Each fingerprint pins the invariant code, PR number, head SHA and review IDs, so an entry
stops matching the moment the PR is pushed to or another review lands — a baselined PR that
comes back to life is re-audited automatically. Entries are therefore expected to go stale;
the guard warns about ones that match nothing and pruning them never changes the verdict.
Adding an entry suppresses a real finding: name the PR, the owning issue, and why.
Empty since BLO-25764 (2026-09-23). Six entries were removed: four I1 and two I3. The reason that
covers all six is head supersession — every baselined head had moved (#1304 -> 2687a148, #1360 ->
66782c03, #1525 -> 7745835e all merged; #1316 pushed to cd7e0c84), and a fingerprint embeds the
head, so none of them can match again. Separately, the I1 shape four of them suppressed is no
longer a violation when the bodies differ (a re-review supersedes); that exemption is I1-only and
does not reach I3, which asserts one canonical body and a matching attestation.
